seismicity is strongly correlated with the local frictional properties and the final size of earthquakes depends on the local physical properties of the fault at the earthquake nucleation sites.
seismicity and stress patterns are significantly correlated with small-scale properties of the fault and that this correlation is a function of the range of size scales of the model parameters.
seismicity is correlated with small-scale heterogeneities and the scaling properties of seismicity are self-similar.

a number of questions: 1.
the statistical properties of seismicity and their dependence on the heterogeneity of fault zone properties at various evolutionary stages.
the seismic response of faults with a range of heterogeneity and the statistical properties of the resulting seismicity.

the observed scaling relations are not a result of a particular choice of the employed friction law or the employed model realization.
the seismicity of a fault zone at different evolutionary stages is governed by a combination of the large-scale and small-scale physical properties of the fault zone.

seismicity is controlled by a combination of small scale frictional properties and large scale properties of the fault zone, with the former dominating at early stages of evolution and the latter at later stages.

the seismicity and the stress field in the fault zone are strongly correlated.
the seismic response of the fault is governed mainly by the local properties of the fault.
the seismic response of fault systems is controlled by the physical properties at the small scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the statistical properties of seismicity are controlled by the physical properties of the fault zone.

the seismic response of fault zones at various evolutionary stages can be described by the same statistical functions, which are determined by a combination of the physical properties at the nucleation sites of large earthquakes.

the statistical properties of seismicity are strongly dependent on the spatial distribution of model parameters, and that the spatial distribution of these parameters is a function of the evolutionary stage of the fault.
